items.summary: In an opinion dated October 26, 2026, the Seventh Circuit affirmed the judgment of conviction of Dan R. Waeckerle, Jr. on four counts, including soliciting and transferring obscene material to a minor and sexual exploitation of a minor, and the resulting 485-month sentence. The court held that circumstantial evidence, including text messages and phone logs, was sufficient for a jury to find the solicited and transferred material obscene under Miller v. California. The court also addressed Waeckerle's challenges to the exclusion of evidence of the minor's prior sexual history under Federal Rule of Evidence 412, the excusal of a juror during deliberations, and the seating of an alternate juror.

Dodd challenged the sentence as procedurally and substantively unreasonable, including the five-level pattern enhancement under U.S.S.G. § 2G2.2(b)(5) based on a prior juvenile conviction. The court stated that any procedural error would be harmless and that the sentence fell within the scope of the district court's discretion.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–125: To allow a period in which members of the clergy may revoke their exemption from Social Security coverage, and for other purposes. Public Law 125 Public Law 119–125 140 Stat. 1076 2026-10-20 2026-10-20 United States Gove
items.summary: Public Law 119-125, the Clergy Act, allows ordained ministers, members of religious orders, and Christian Science practitioners who hold an exemption from Social Security coverage under section 1402(e)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code to revoke that exemption by filing an application with the Commissioner of Internal Revenue by the applicable tax return due date. Revocations take effect for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028, and applicants may not later re-elect the exemption. The Act also requires the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, in consultation with the Commissioner of Social Security, to submit to Congress within 90 days of enactment a plan to inform affected individuals of their eligibility to revoke the exemption.
items.title: Public Law 119–125: To allow a period in which members of the clergy may revoke their exemption from Social Security coverage, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–126: To require the Secretary of Agriculture to convey the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site to Gila County, Arizona. Public Law 126 Public Law 119–126 140 Stat. 1078 2026-10-20 2026-10-20 United States Gove
items.summary: Public Law 119-126 directs the Secretary of Agriculture, acting through the Forest Service, to convey approximately 232.9 acres of Tonto National Forest land in the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site to Gila County, Arizona, if the county submits a written request within 180 days of enactment. The conveyance is to be made without consideration by quitclaim deed, subject to valid existing rights, and at the county's expense for surveys and required environmental and resource analyses. The land must be used only for serving and supporting veterans of the Armed Forces, and it reverts to the United States at the Secretary's discretion if used otherwise.
items.title: Public Law 119–126: To require the Secretary of Agriculture to convey the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site to Gila County, Arizona.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–127: To direct the Secretary of Commerce to conduct a study on the feasibility of manufacturing in the United States products for critical infrastructure sectors, and for other purposes. Public Law 127 Public Law 119–127 140
items.summary: Public Law 119-127, the Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act, directs the Secretary of Commerce to study, within one year of enactment, products in each of the 16 critical infrastructure sectors that are in high demand and imported due to manufacturing, material, or supply chain constraints. The study is to analyze the costs, benefits, and effects on jobs and product prices of manufacturing those products in the United States, including in rural areas and industrial parks. The Secretary must submit a report with recommendations to Congress within 18 months of enactment and post it publicly on the Department of Commerce website, and the Act does not authorize the Secretary to compel information from any person.
items.title: Public Law 119–127: To direct the Secretary of Commerce to conduct a study on the feasibility of manufacturing in the United States products for critical infrastructure sectors, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–129: To require online dating service providers to provide fraud ban notifications to online dating service members, and for other purposes. Public Law 129 Public Law 119–129 140 Stat. 1084 2026-10-20 2026-10-20 United States
items.summary: Public Law 119-129, the Romance Scam Prevention Act, requires online dating service providers to send a fraud ban notification to any member who has received a message from a banned member, generally within 24 hours of the ban, with extensions at the provider's judgment or at a law enforcement official's request. Each notification must be clear and conspicuous, sent by email or text message, and include specified contents such as the banned member's profile identifier, a warning against sending cash or financial information, and provider contact information. The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general may enforce the Act, and the Act preempts state laws that govern whether or how providers must give such notifications. The Act takes effect one year after enactment.
items.title: Public Law 119–129: To require online dating service providers to provide fraud ban notifications to online dating service members, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–131: To direct the Secretary of Labor to train certain employees of Department of Labor how to effectively detect and assist law enforcement in preventing human trafficking during the course of their official duties, and for
items.summary: Public Law 119-131, the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act, directs the Secretary of Labor to implement, within 180 days of enactment, a program of training and periodic continuing education for Department of Labor employees on detecting human trafficking and referring suspected cases. The training is to cover methods for identifying suspected victims and traffickers, a referral course of action to the Department of Justice and other authorities, and an evaluation of the training, with the Wage and Hour Division training considering states with significant increases in oppressive child labor. The Secretary must report annually to the House Committee on Education and Workforce and the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions on the training provided, its effectiveness, and the number of referred cases.
items.title: Public Law 119–131: To direct the Secretary of Labor to train certain employees of Department of Labor how to effectively detect and assist law enforcement in preventing human trafficking during the course of their official duties, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–132: To modify the boundary of the Vicksburg National Military Park in the State of Mississippi, and for other purposes. Public Law 132 Public Law 119–132 140 Stat. 1093 2026-10-20 2026-10-20 United States Government Publishi
items.summary: Public Law 119-132, the Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary Modification Act, directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the State of Mississippi, by quitclaim deed and without consideration, two parcels of federal land within Vicksburg National Military Park totaling approximately 7.43 acres, as depicted on maps dated September 2024. Upon conveyance, the Secretary must modify the park boundary to exclude the conveyed land. The conveyed land must be used to facilitate public access to the park and enhance the visitor experience in a manner consistent with the park's interpretive mission, and it is subject to any use restrictions the Secretary determines to be appropriate.
items.title: Public Law 119–132: To modify the boundary of the Vicksburg National Military Park in the State of Mississippi, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–134: To amend the Mineral Leasing Act to extend the period of time during which the Secretary of the Interior is required to collect a fee for each new application for a permit to drill, and for other purposes. Public Law 134
items.summary: Public Law 119–134, cited as the "License to Drill Act," was approved October 20, 2026, and amends Section 35(d) of the Mineral Leasing Act (30 U.S.C. 191(d)). The amendments replace references to 2026 with 2037 in paragraphs (1) and (4), extending the period during which the Secretary of the Interior is required to collect a fee for each new application for a permit to drill. Paragraph (3) is revised to direct the transfer, for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2037, of all fees collected under the subsection to the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund.
items.title: Public Law 119–134: To amend the Mineral Leasing Act to extend the period of time during which the Secretary of the Interior is required to collect a fee for each new application for a permit to drill, and for other purposes.

items.summary: This final rule revises regulations for hunting and trapping seasons, harvest limits, and methods and means related to taking of wildlife for subsistence uses during the 2026-27 and 2027-28 regulatory years. The Federal Subsistence Board (hereafter referred to as “the Board”) is on a schedule of completing the process of revising subsistence taking of wildlife regulations in even-numbered years and subsistence taking of fish and shellfish regulations in odd-numbered years; public proposal and review processes take place during the preceding year. The Board also addresses customary and traditional use determinations during the applicable cycle. This final rule revises the existing subsistence wildlife taking regulations, the general regulations on subsistence taking of fish and wildlife, customary and traditional use determinations, and addresses a deferred proposal regarding eulachon harvest in District 1 from the last fish cycle and a deferred proposal regarding brown bear hide sales from the last wildlife cycle. This final rule also makes administrative corrections to the regulations and corrects errors discovered since the last rulemaking.
items.title: Subsistence Management Regulations for Public Lands in Alaska—2026-27 and 2027-28 Subsistence Taking of Wildlife Regulations

items.summary: The National Mediation Board (NMB) is issuing this final rule; technical amendment to amend its regulations to reflect a change in address for its Washington, DC headquarters office. This technical amendment is a nomenclature change that replaces outdated addresses with the NMB's current headquarters address. Additionally, this final rule amends the NMB's regulations to eliminate references to the NMB Chief of Staff position, a position that no longer exists in the agency's organization. This action is administrative, technical, and editorial in nature; is necessary to provide accuracy and clarity to the NMB's Rules; and does not alter the rights, duties, or obligations of the public.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-11817; Project Identifier AD-2026-01020-E] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. Engines AGENCY: Federal Aviation Adm
items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all CFM International, S.A. (CFM) Model CFM56-7B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by an event involving a CFM Model CFM56-7B26/3 engine where a fan blade separated and resulted in an engine in-flight shutdown (IFSD) with debris penetrating the fuselage, which caused a loss of pressurization and prompted an emergency descent. This proposed AD would require a visual inspection of the fan blades for findings considered not serviceable and, depending on the results of the inspection, replacement with a serviceable part and additional fan blade inspections. This proposed AD would also require sending the inspection results to CFM if any finding considered not serviceable is found. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. Engines

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Model SA 365 N helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of tightening torque loss on the input flange nut due to circular wear on the faces of the flange, the slip ring, and the input flange. This condition, if not addressed, could lead to degradation or jamming of the input roller bearings and loss of yaw control of the helicopter. This AD requires repetitive functional inspections (checks) and, depending on the results of the inspections, corrective actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-1326; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-00312-R; Amendment 39-23498; AD 2026-21-09] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deuts
items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3, EC635T2+, MBB-BK 117 C-2, and MBB-BK 117 D-2 helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of cracks on the cable drum of the rescue hoist assembly. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the cable drum of certain rescue hoist assemblies for cracks and, depending on the results, replacing or repairing the cable drum of the rescue hoist assembly. This AD also prohibits the operation and the installation of an affected rescue hoist assembly on a helicopter, unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B2, AS350B3, AS355N, AS355NP, and EC130B4 helicopters. This AD was prompted by a report of a release of the load on the cargo hook without manual release initiation by the pilot. This AD requires inspecting the load dropping control system, inspecting the manual release lever for free play, and, depending on the results, performing corrective actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 737-700, -700C, -800, and -900ER series airplanes. This AD was prompted by a leak through the form-in-place (FiP) gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel found during a leak check. This AD requires a detailed inspection of the left- and right-side FiP gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for correct sealant installation, a fluid leak test of the engine fuel shutoff valve access panels for any leak, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 737-8, 737-9, and 737-8200 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a leak through the form-in-place (FiP) gasket found during a leak check. This AD requires a detailed inspection of the FiP gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for correct sealant installation, or a detailed inspection at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for any damage on the preformed seal, depending on configuration; a fluid leak test of the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for any leak; and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-2723; Project Identifier AD-2024-00429-A; Amendment 39-23502; AD 2026-21-13] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Ontic Engineering and Manu
items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. Model SA226-T, SA226-AT, SA226-T(B), SA226-TC, SA227-AC (C-26A), SA227-AT, SA227-BC (C-26A), SA227-PC, SA227-CC, SA227-DC (C-26B), and SA227-TT (300) airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of in-flight pitch trim actuator failures. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the pitch trim actuator for cracked, missing, or compromised sealant, replacing and sealing the pitch trim actuator if cracked, missing, or compromised, repetitively measuring the pitch trim actuator travel time, and depending on the results of the measurements, replacing and sealing the pitch trim actuator. This AD also requires certain pitch trim actuators to be sealed after installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. (Type Certificate Previously Held by Swearingen, Fairchild Aircraft, and M7 Aerospace) Airplanes

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 25 [Docket No. FAA-2026-10627; Notice No. 25-898-SC] Special Conditions: Embraer S.A. Model ERJ 190-400 Airplane; Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System AGENCY: Federal Aviat
items.summary: This action proposes special conditions for the Embraer S.A. (Embraer) Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane. This airplane will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for transport category airplanes. This design feature is a functionality known as the Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System (E 2 TS). The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These proposed special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.
items.title: Special Conditions: Embraer S.A. Model ERJ 190-400 Airplane; Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System

items.summary: The Coast Guard is proposing to amend the Southern California Firework Events for Los Angeles-Long Beach Captain of the Port Zone Annual Safety Zones. The Coast Guard proposes eight new events to be added, thirteen events to be updated, and two events removed. The safety zones are needed to protect waterways users and keep them clear of potentially harmful debris within the fallout zone. This proposed rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from being in the safety zone unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port Los Angeles-Long Beach. We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking.

items.summary: The United States Department of Justice (“Department”) is amending several of its regulations pertaining to the National Instant Criminal Background Check System (“NICS” or “system”) of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”) to authorize Federal Firearm Licensees (“FFLs” or “licensees”) to use NICS for purposes of voluntarily conducting employment background checks relating to certain current or prospective FFL employees. This final rule describes in more detail how, upon its effective date, FFLs will be able to conduct “firearm handler background checks” (“FHCs”) of “eligible employees.”
items.title: Bipartisan Safer Communities Act of 2022—Criteria for National Instant Criminal Background Check System (“NICS”) Background Checks of Firearm Handlers

items.summary: PHMSA proposes to update the Hazardous Materials Regulations to adopt certain international regulations and standards related to proper shipping names, hazard classes, packing groups, special provisions, packaging authorizations, air transport quantity limitations, and vessel stowage requirements. items.title: Hazardous Materials: Harmonization With International Standards

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE 28 CFR Part 106 [JMD Docket No. 157; A.G. Order No. 7256-2026] RIN 1105-AB71 Implementation of HAVANA Act of 2021 AGENCY: Department of Justice. ACTION: Final rule. SUMMARY: On April 19, 2024, the Department of Justice
items.summary: On April 19, 2024, the Department of Justice published an interim final rule to implement the HAVANA Act of 2021. No comments were received on the interim final rule. The HAVANA Act authorizes agency heads to provide payments to certain individuals who have incurred qualifying injuries to the brain. This final rule adopts the interim final rule with minor, non-substantive changes to the titles of certain officials involved in the payment review process and the earliest eligibility date for claims in accordance with statutory changes occurring after issuance of the interim final rule. This rule covers current and former Department of Justice employees and their dependents.
items.title: Implementation of HAVANA Act of 2021

labels.items: ALL observed items including backfill — filter on is_backfill=false to match the human page's listing
